new_findings.title: Cookie-authenticated image requests lose viewer identity without a REST nonce
new_findings.defect: Signed image URLs contain expires and token but no _wpnonce (class-blob-url-rewriter.php:144-150). WordPress REST cookie authentication sets the current user to 0 when no nonce is present, then returns success; the route-scoped filter only handles rest_cookie_invalid_nonce and does not restore the viewer. verify_blob_token therefore rejects the legitimate image request with 401. See [WordPress source](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/rest_cookie_check_errors/).
new_findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated admin page renders a signed recognition blob URL in an img element. The browser sends the login cookie but no REST nonce, WordPress clears the current user, and verify_blob_token returns 401 so the blob or thumbnail does not display.
new_findings.fix: Append wp_create_nonce('wp_rest') as _wpnonce to each signed proxy URL in BlobUrlRewriter and add an integration test that runs the image request through the REST cookie-authentication filter before verify_blob_token.
